title: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight
hook: Duryodhana offers the earth; Yudhishthira refuses it, and makes a risky offer of his own
carry: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight
tomorrow: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight

segments.voice: Your line was Shalya, and yesterday Duryodhana lay hidden in the lake until some hunters gave him away. What did you find you'd been hiding under the surface? Day eight hundred forty-six.

An offer rises from under the water. Take the whole earth, Duryodhana says, in effect. My friends are dead, my brothers are dead. I have no wish to rule an empty kingdom. I'll go to the forest, dressed in deerskins, and live there. The kingdom is yours. It sounds like surrender. It sounds like the end of the war, handed over without another blow. And Yudhishthira, standing on the bank, refuses. Today, why he won't take it, and the risky thing he offers instead.
screen: `TAKE THE WHOLE EARTH.` → `I'LL GO TO THE FOREST.` → `YUDHISHTHIRA REFUSES.`

segments.voice: It isn't yours to give, Yudhishthira answers, in Ganguli's telling. When we asked for land before the war, you wouldn't give us as much ground as the point of a needle would cover. Now that you've lost it, you offer it all as a gift? A warrior doesn't take a kingdom as charity. Come out and fight. Then Yudhishthira goes further, and it gets dangerous. Choose any one of us, he says, with any weapon you like. Beat that one, and the kingdom is yours. Krishna is alarmed. He tells Yudhishthira he has put everything at risk again, on a single throw, and that none of the brothers but Bhima can match Duryodhana with the mace, and even Bhima has less skill. Some readers hear in this the old dice game coming back. The king who lost everything once by gambling has just gambled again. Duryodhana rises out of the lake, dripping, wounded, mace on his shoulder, and he chooses the mace. And Bhima steps forward to meet him. The fight is agreed. Two cousins who have hated each other since boyhood will settle it alone, with everyone else watching.
screen: `IT ISN'T YOURS TO GIVE` · `CHOOSE ANY ONE OF US` · `KRISHNA IS ALARMED` · then, large: `DURYODHANA RISES`

segments.voice: Sit, and rest your hands open in your lap. Breathe in. Breathe out. Bring to mind a time you offered something only after you'd already lost it, or were offered something that way. Notice how the offer felt from each side. Don't judge it. Breathe in, and let your hands stay open. Breathe out, and let your shoulders drop. If you pray, you can bring that memory into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Shalya. An offer refused at the lake's edge, a gamble made, and a king rising from the water to fight.
Your line: Shalya, Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight. Today, before you make a bold offer, take one breath and count what it puts at risk. Day eight hundred forty-six.

howItsDone: The exchange at the lake, from the Shalya Parva, is retold in readings and serials of the Mahabharata, and Duryodhana's earlier refusal of even a needle's point of land is recalled there.

myth: Yudhishthira accepted the kingdom Duryodhana offered from the lake
he refused it: it wasn't Duryodhana's to give, and a warrior doesn't take a kingdom as charity.
Yudhishthira let Duryodhana choose his opponent and his weapon
and Krishna was alarmed at the risk.
Duryodhana chose the mace when he came out of the lake
and Bhima stepped forward to meet him.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira. your beaten cousin offers you the whole kingdom from under the water. what do you do?
options: accept it, and end the war.
refuse it, and offer a fight against any one brother, any weapon.
order the army to drain the lake.
fork.reveal: Yudhishthira refuses the gift and offers a single fight on Duryodhana's terms. Krishna is alarmed, and Duryodhana rises with his mace.

original.note: mace: the weapon Duryodhana chooses when he rises from the lake.

trapdoor: what you thought: Duryodhana surrendered at the lake.
what it means: he offered the kingdom, and Yudhishthira refused, because it was no longer his to give.
what a scholar hears: Yudhishthira's offer to stake everything on one fight is a second gamble, and some readers hear the dice game coming back.
